minutes.headline: Sewer Commission set a Feb 2 budget workshop and deferred a vote on the town counsel access policy.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a school facilities director dispute a sewer bill tied to irrigation meter readings and agreed to wait another billing cycle. It reviewed the 384 Mass Ave connection with the contractor, who will provide a survey plan, and received the first FY22 draft sewer budget. A vote on changing the counsel-access policy was withdrawn until the full commission is present; the minutes of the prior meeting were approved.

what_happened.line: The commission withdrew a motion to change town counsel access from notification to permission and postponed the vote until the full commission is present.
A budget workshop was set for February 2, with the regular February 9 meeting to review and try to finalize the FY22 sewer budget.
The business manager presented the first FY22 draft sewer budget, including a part-time assistant position that needs personnel committee and town meeting approval.
The commission agreed to wait through the next billing cycle before adjusting the school's disputed sewer bill, and the facilities director accepted.
The 384 Mass Ave contractor will submit a survey and engineer plan to complete the items in the commission's letter.

why_it_matters: The FY22 draft sets the sewer rates and fees that feed into residents' sewer bills, and the new assistant position would add a recurring cost that town meeting must approve.

The deferred counsel-access vote decides whether commissioners can use town counsel's office hours as of right or only with permission, which affects how freely the board can get legal advice on sewer matters.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main decisions: the withdrawn counsel access motion, the 2/2 workshop and 2/9 finalization, the school waiting a cycle, and the $30,929.43 capital reserve transfer noted without a vote. They differ on the retained earnings figure (ours garbled it, the official says $7,800), the school usage figure (12,430 vs 12,436 cu.ft.), and who sends the Fitchburg extension request. The official minutes also record Carl Luck's betterment comment and several action items that ours leave out.
